correctness.rationale: The forcing proof closes the higher-arity gap. If a condition forced a nonidentity automorphism, dense free-amalgamation separation shows it must move a point in every infinite ground-model block. Choose uncountably many disjoint countable blocks, strengthen to decide moved points \(s_\xi\) and images \(t_\xi\), and apply the Delta-system lemma to the finite supports. After thinning, all conditions agree on the finite root. Sources lie in petals; images can also be forced into petals, because two distinct sources mapped to the same root point would be compatible and contradict injectivity. Selecting \(n\) petals makes both the source \(n\)-set and image \(n\)-set fresh cross-petal sets. Free amalgamation can assign opposite truth values to those two relation instances while preserving all decided images, contradicting relation preservation. The argument uses distinct coordinates, so conventions about repeated tuples are immaterial.
residual_risks: The theorem is relative to the stated finite-condition generic forcing and does not assert later-forcing absoluteness.
